newsitem.title: INDIA: MTNL offices gutted in Delhi fire.
newsitem.headline: MTNL offices gutted in Delhi fire.

text.p: India's state-owned Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) said on Tuesday that two of its offices were gutted in a fire in the capital, but its telephone services were unaffected.
Fire erupted on the ninth floor of the Chandralok Building of New Delhi's Connaught Place area in the morning.
The ninth floor houses the office of MTNL's chief civil engineer's office and on the tenth floor is the state-owned unit's training centre for telephone operators.
L. Balasubramaniam, an engineer at the MTNL office in the building, said the offices were "completely gutted".
"There are not many equipments there on the two floors," MTNL chairman S. Rajagopalan said, adding that the monetary cost of damages had not yet been determined.
The building also houses the offices of the State Bank of India, Shipping Corporation of India, Essar Group, the tourism offices of several northern Indian states and Japan Airlines Co Ltd.
Essar said earlier on Tuesday that the fire had knocked out its cellular telephone services but they were quickly restored.
